lecture_context.lecture_title: What’s Going On Inside My Model?

unit.name: CNN saliency maps and integrated gradients
unit.description: Explains pixel-level gradient attribution for CNN image classifiers and extends it with integrated gradients along a baseline-to-image path.
unit.summary: For the zoo classifier case, the lecture first motivates explanations that show whether a model is looking at the relevant image region rather than merely outputting a class probability [ts=891s] [ts=1053s]. A saliency map is built by differentiating a class score such as dog with respect to the input pixels, so bright pixels are the ones whose perturbation most affects the score [ts=1212s] [ts=1259s]. The instructor emphasizes using the pre-softmax class score rather than the post-softmax probability because post-softmax depends on all competing class scores [ts=1280s] [ts=1315s]. Integrated gradients are presented as a more common extension that accumulates gradients along a path from a black baseline image to the actual image, with a retina-lesion example showing attribution concentrated near the annotated lesion [ts=1416s] [ts=1467s].

key_points.text: Saliency maps compute the derivative of a chosen pre-softmax class score with respect to the input image.
High-gradient pixels indicate where pixel changes would most change the selected class score.
Pre-softmax scores are preferred for saliency because post-softmax probabilities also change when other class scores change.
A saliency map whose bright pixels are scattered away from the object suggests the model may be getting lucky rather than looking at the right place.
Integrated gradients interpolate from a baseline image to the actual image and accumulates gradients along that path.
In the retina example, integrated gradients highlight the lesion regions used for the prediction.

kp_catalog.name: Saliency via input gradients
kp_catalog.description: Saliency maps identify input pixels that most affect a chosen class score by differentiating the score with respect to the input image.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because saliency via input gradients clarifies saliency maps identify input pixels that most affect a chosen class score by differentiating the score with respect to the input image, sharpening later modeling, analysis, or evaluation choices.

kp_catalog.name: Integrated gradients
kp_catalog.description: An attribution method that accumulates gradients along an interpolation path from a baseline input to the actual input.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The lecture presents integrated gradients as a more common extension of saliency maps, but does not go deeply into the derivation [ts=1416s] [ts=1452s].
